literal: Investigating the prognostication: "It is famine; the five grains are not stored."
idiomatic: Commentary reads famine and empty granaries.

literal: That month, great drought and famine.
idiomatic: That month brought drought and hunger.

literal: On the new moon of day Gengwu in the sixth year’s second month, there was a shooting star large as a dipper, its light shining on the ground, issuing from the Celestial Market, moving west into the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Year six, second month, gengwu new moon: a dipper-bright meteor left the Market and plunged west into the enclosure.

literal: The prognostication states: "A great man will answer for it."
idiomatic: A magnate bears the sign.

literal: In the eighth year’s sixth month, Emperor Cheng died.
idiomatic: Year eight, June: Emperor Cheng died.

literal: In Emperor Mu’s sixth month, day Xinsi, before the sun had set, there was a shooting star large as three dipper-ladles, from above Chen and Si, moving southeast.
idiomatic: Mudi, June, xinsi, before sunset: a triple-dipper meteor rose from the Chen-Si quadrant southeastward.

literal: By gnomon reckoning it lay between the Sieve and Dipper, probably Yan’s division.
idiomatic: Shadow reckoning placed it between Sieve and Dipper in Yan’s field.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "It is Camp Head."
idiomatic: The books again call it Camp Head.

literal: Below Camp Head, blood flows in torrents."
idiomatic: Under Camp Head comes a blood tide."

literal: At the time Murong Jun falsely styled himself Great Yan, attacking without cease.
idiomatic: Murong Jun then claimed Great Yan and raided endlessly.

literal: On day Guiwei in the tenth year’s fourth month, there was a shooting star large as a dipper, red-yellow in color, issuing from the Weaving Girl, sinking in Zaofu, with sound like thunder.
idiomatic: Year ten, April, guiwei: a dipper-sized red-yellow meteor ran Weaving Girl to Zaofu with thunder.

literal: The prognostication states: "Yan and Qi will have arms; the hundred surnames will flee in exile."
idiomatic: Yan-Qi war drives commoners into exile.

literal: That year’s twelfth month, Murong Jun then occupied Linzhang and wholly held You, Bing, Qing, and Ji.
idiomatic: That December Murong Jun took Linzhang and held You, Bing, Qing, and Ji.

literal: The various generals along the Yellow River scattered in flight; river fords were cut off.
idiomatic: River generals fled and crossings closed.

literal: Murong Ke attacked Qi.
idiomatic: Murong Ke struck Qi.

literal: In the eleventh month, a crooked arrow flowed from southeast to northwest, its length half the sky.
idiomatic: November: a crooked-arrow comet crossed half the sky northwestward.

literal: On day Gengxu in the fourth year’s tenth month, the Celestial Dog was seen in the southwest.
idiomatic: Year four, October, gengxu: the Celestial Dog appeared southwest.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be great arms and flowing blood."
idiomatic: Great battles and bloodshed follow.

literal: In Haixi’s tenth month, day Renshen, there was a great shooting star moving west down, with sound like thunder.
idiomatic: Haixi reign, October, renshen: a huge western fireball boomed.

literal: The next year, an envoy was dispatched to degrade Yuan Zhen to commoner status.
idiomatic: Next year envoys stripped Yuan Zhen of rank.

literal: Huan Wen was at Shou-chun; Zhen died of illness; his heir Jin succeeded and begged rescue from Fu Jian.
idiomatic: Huan Wen held Shouyang; Yuan Zhen died and his son Jin sought Fu Jian’s aid.

literal: Wen defeated Fu Jian’s army.
idiomatic: Huan Wen broke Fu Jian’s relief column.

literal: In the sixth year, Shouyang city fell.
idiomatic: Year six: Shouyang fell.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowu’s tenth month, day Yimao, there was a racing star moving southeast through Wings and Chariot, with sound like thunder.
idiomatic: Xiaowudi, October, yimao: a bolide roared southeast through Wings and Chariot.

literal: The prognostication states: "Chu lands will have arms; the army will be broken; the hundred surnames will flee in exile."
idiomatic: Chu sees defeat, rout, and refugee columns.

literal: In the twelfth month, Fu Jian’s Jing inspector Liang Cheng and Xiangyang defender Yan Zhen led a host to campaign against Jingling; Huan Shiqian greatly defeated them, captured Yan Zhen alive, beheaded seven thousand, and took ten thousand captives.
idiomatic: December: Fu Jian’s Liang Cheng and Yan Zhen struck Jingling until Huan Shiqian shattered them, taking Yan Zhen and seven thousand heads.

literal: Sound like thunder is an image of generals’ anger.
idiomatic: The thunder images generals’ fury.

literal: On day Wuchen in the thirteenth year’s intercalary month, the Celestial Dog dropped northeast with sound.
idiomatic: Year thirteen, leap month, wuchen: the Celestial Dog fell northeast audibly.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be a great battle and flowing blood."
idiomatic: Major bloodshed follows.

literal: From this time Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong all blocked roads with arms and vied for supremacy.
idiomatic: Afterward Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong kept private armies.

literal: In the fourteenth year’s first month, Pengcheng’s occult bandits again falsely styled a title at Huangqiu; Liu Laozhi destroyed them.
idiomatic: Fourteenth year, first month: Pengcheng rebels styled themselves at Huangqiu until Liu Laozhi wiped them out.

literal: In the third month, Zhang Dao broke Hexiang and Taishan; Xiang Qinzhi drove him off.
idiomatic: March: Zhang Dao hit Hexiang and Taishan until Xiang Qinzhi repulsed him.

literal: On day Jiayin in Emperor An’s third month, red shooting stars, numerous, moved west, passing Oxherd, Emptiness, Rooftops, Celestial Ford, Forbidden Passage, piercing the Supreme Palace Enclosure and Purple Palace.
idiomatic: Emperor An, third month, jiayin: many red meteors streamed west through key asterisms into the enclosure and Purple Palace.

literal: The prognostication states: "Stars are the likeness of commoners; numerous ones moving west are an image of many generals flowing west."
idiomatic: Meteors image commoners; a western swarm means columns fleeing west.

literal: Passing the Son of Heaven’s court means the ruler is weak and ministers strong; feudal lords’ troops are unchecked."
idiomatic: Crossing the celestial court shows a feeble throne, mighty ministers, and uncontrollable regional armies."

literal: That year’s fifth month, Sun En raided Wu commandery and killed the interior governor.
idiomatic: That May Sun En hit Wu commandery and slew its governor.

literal: In the sixth month, he reached Jingkou.
idiomatic: June: he reached Jingkou.

literal: Thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert; camps and formations garrisoned and held; Liu Yu pursued and broke him.
idiomatic: The capital region armed; Liu Yu chased and crushed Sun En.

literal: In the first Yuanxing year’s seventh month, great famine; men ate one another.
idiomatic: Yuanxing one, July: famine drove cannibalism.

literal: East of the Zhe River six or seven tenths fled; Wu commandery and Wu-xing lost half their households; those who fled west also counted in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: East of Zhe six or seven in ten fled; Wu and Wu-xing halved; tens of thousands bolted west.

literal: In the tenth month, Huan Xuan dispatched a general to strike Liu Gui, defeated him, and drove him off.
idiomatic: October: Huan Xuan’s column routed Liu Gui.

literal: Gui fled to Qing Province.
idiomatic: Liu Gui fled to Qingzhou.

literal: Cloud vapors
idiomatic: Anomalous cloud vapors

literal: In Emperor Hui’s twelfth month, day Renyin night, there was red vapor spanning the sky, rumbling with hidden sound.
idiomatic: Huidi, December, renyin night: red qi bridged the sky with low thunder.

literal: In the second year’s tenth month, day Dingchou, red vapor appeared in the north, east and west spanning the sky.
idiomatic: Year two, October, dingchou: northern red qi stretched horizon to horizon.

literal: The prognostication states: "Both mean great arms."
idiomatic: Both signs mean major war.

literal: Rumbling with hidden sound is an image of anger.
idiomatic: The rumble images wrath.

literal: Afterward the four seas were cloud-turbulent and the nine domains crossed arms.
idiomatic: Then the realm boiled in war on every border.

literal: On day Jiashen in the twelfth month, there was white vapor like a rainbow, from mid-sky north down to the ground, seen five nights then extinguished.
idiomatic: December, jiashen: white arc from zenith to earth lasted five nights.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great arms will arise."
idiomatic: Major war follows.

literal: The next year, Wang Mi rose in Qing and Xu, Ji Sang threw Hebei into chaos, and poison spread under Heaven.
idiomatic: Next year Wang Mi and Ji Sang’s risings poisoned the realm.

literal: In Emperor Huai’s eleventh month, day Yihai, there was white vapor like a belt, two each issuing south and north from ground to sky, piercing Orion’s Belt and the伐 stars.
idiomatic: Huaidi, November, yihai: paired white belts crossed Orion’s Blade.

literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven great arms will arise."
idiomatic: Realm-wide war is portended.

literal: In the fourth year’s third month, Sima Yue arrested Miao Yin and others.
idiomatic: Year four, March: Sima Yue seized Miao Yin and company.

literal: Moreover, the three fronts were cloud-turbulent, attacking without cease.
idiomatic: Three war zones seethed without pause.

literal: In the fifth year’s third month, Sima Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le broke his host; the dead exceeded one hundred thousand.
idiomatic: Year five, March: Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le annihilated his army, killing over a hundred thousand.

literal: In the sixth month, the capital was burned out; the emperor went to the barbarian court.
idiomatic: June: Luoyang burned and the emperor fell captive.

literal: In Emperor Min’s tenth month, day Jisi night, red vapor blazed in the northwest.
idiomatic: Mindi, October, jisi night: red qi flared northwest.

literal: Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan campaigned against Du Tao’s faction at Stone City and was defeated.
idiomatic: Jing inspector Tao Kan attacked Du Tao’s allies at Stone City and lost.
